hook: The count who wrote War and Peace, then tried to live like a peasant and preached non-violence.

pages.x: Leo Tolstoy was born in 1828 at Yasnaya Polyana, his family's estate south of Moscow. By nine he had lost both parents. He left university without a degree, gambled, drank and ran up debts.

When he was little, his older brother told him that the secret of how to make all people happy was written on a green stick, buried at the edge of a ravine on the estate. Tolstoy asked to be buried there, and he was.
He joined the army, and in the Crimean War fought in the siege of Sevastopol. His sketches of the fighting, showing the horror of war, made him famous in Russia.

From 1863 to 1869 he wrote War and Peace, a huge novel of Russia in the time of Napoleon's invasion, with more than 500 characters. His wife Sophia copied out his messy drafts by hand again and again.
Anna Karenina, finished in 1877, begins: "Happy families are all alike; every unhappy family is unhappy in its own way." Many writers call it the greatest novel ever written.

In his fifties, rich and famous, he fell into despair about the meaning of life. He turned to a simple faith of love and non-violence, gave up meat, drink and hunting, dressed like a peasant and worked in the fields.

pages.t: Do not resist evil with violence
pages.x: His book The Kingdom of God Is Within You, of 1894, preached resisting evil without violence. It was banned in Russia, and in 1901 the Church cast him out. A young lawyer in South Africa, Gandhi, read it and was changed.
pages.img: The Kingdom of God Is Within You

pages.x: At 82, after years of quarrels with his wife over his will, he left home secretly one night in 1910. He fell ill on the train, and died at the little station of Astapovo, while reporters crowded outside.
Tolstoy is one of the greatest novelists who ever lived, and his teaching of non-violence inspired Gandhi and Martin Luther King.
pts: Wrote War and Peace and Anna Karenina
